decision: D3: effective authority = Host policy ∩ Mission authorization ∩ Agent envelope ∩ device permissions ∩ exact Host-offered operation. A narrowed Agent consent is not restored by a one-time device answer; valid in-scope one-time answers keep working.
source: F01 §7 item 3 (round-4 HIGH disposition): nine T9/T9R tests encoded "a device may answer a one-time ask for an Agent planned file step after the workstation narrowed the consent".
method: Each test was inspected individually. None was deleted or skipped and no assertion was inverted. Each fixture that relied on narrowing was changed to an in-scope ask_every_time grant, so the original property (exact offer, stale revision refused, substitution refused, race resolves once, ...) is still asserted on a valid answer. A device write now lands only after a workstation promotion. Negative regressions assert that the narrowed case is refused.

tests.originalRequirement: F12-F15: device answers only exact Host offers; stale revision refused; F19-F22/F50: Pause/Resume reissue asks at the current revision; a device write answer lands only inside the owner's consent.
tests.before: Agent consent narrowed by adjust removing filesystem.write; asserted the write ask is answerable remotely and that device allow_once writes result.txt directly.
tests.after: Consent keeps filesystem.write plus a workstation capability.grant filesystem.write ask_every_time; the stale-revision check uses a non-narrowing adjust (maximumActions 10); device allow_once is staged, a device promotion attempt is WORKSTATION_REQUIRED, the workstation promotes, then result.txt is asserted.
tests.authorizationRationale: F02 D3: a device may not answer a write outside the Agent's current consent; the positive path is kept as an in-scope ask, and F02 D2 requires workstation promotion before the file lands.

tests.originalRequirement: F21: a device answer while the Agent is paused is refused with a reason.
tests.after: status 400, code WORKSTATION_REQUIRED, error is a non-empty reason.
tests.authorizationRationale: The device consent check now runs before the pause message, so the reason text is the generic device refusal. The refusal itself still holds; the assertion keeps the security property and drops the wording that the new order shadows.

tests.test: remote-remediation: all make()-based tests (substitution x3, offline, client-loss, lost-ack, cross-project, four-way, concurrent desktop/phone)
tests.originalRequirement: Device one-time answer on an in-scope write must reach the project only through the Host's reviewed path; a consent-narrowed write must not be answerable.
tests.before: make() narrowed filesystem.write out of consent for every fixture; device allow_once on the write landed the file directly.
tests.after: make() keeps filesystem.write in consent and adds a workstation ask_every_time grant by default; make(name, project, narrowed=true) keeps the old narrowing for the new negative regression. Each positive path calls promoteStaged(f, missionId), which asserts a device cannot promote and that the workstation promotion returns 200 before the file is asserted.
tests.authorizationRationale: F02 D2/D3: device writes are staged and promoted by the workstation; the positive path is an in-scope ask.

tests.test: remote-remediation: T9R remote approval cannot substitute {agentId,missionId,projectId}
tests.originalRequirement: A device answer cannot substitute Agent, Mission or Project; A's consent does not authorize B's resource.
tests.before: device allow_once on A (narrowed) expected 200 and receipt.txt on disk.
tests.after: device allow_once on A (in scope) expected 200; promoteStaged; then receipt.txt = Agent A and project B untouched. The substitution 400 and bus-replay not-allow assertions are unchanged.
tests.authorizationRationale: Positive path moved to a staged, promoted write; the negative checks are unchanged.

tests.test: remote-remediation: T9R offline approval is refused after reconnect
tests.originalRequirement: Stale and replayed approvals are refused; only the fresh Host offer executes.
tests.before: fresh device allow_once expected 200 then receipt.txt.
tests.after: same, plus promoteStaged before the file is asserted.

tests.test: remote-remediation: T9R client-only connection loss during admitted work
tests.originalRequirement: Client-only socket loss does not interrupt Host-side admitted work; same Host epoch; one Agent; one write.
tests.before: HeldFilesystem held filesystem.write (the adapter call the device write now never reaches), so the test awaited fs.entered with no timeout.
tests.after: HeldFilesystem holds filesystem.compare for receipt.txt (the write step's verification, which runs after promotion); promoteStaged precedes; fs.entered is raced against a 15 s timeout.
tests.authorizationRationale: A staged device write never reaches the adapter, so the in-flight work is the verification that runs after promotion. The timeout prevents a silent hang.

tests.test: remote-remediation: T9R F-02 workstation revocation (self sign-out part)
tests.originalRequirement: F02 D5: self sign-out ends the device's own authority; workstation-granted approvals are independent.
tests.before: assert.equal(envelope(signedOut).revokedAt, null) and state ready, documented as keeping the approvals the user gave.
tests.after: assert.ok(envelope(signedOut).revokedAt); state stopped; workstation envelope (owner) still revokedAt null and state ready.
tests.authorizationRationale: New contract: the envelope the device granted is revoked on its own sign-out. The owner-envelope invariant is kept and asserted explicitly. This inverts the legacy assertion deliberately and is safer.

tests.originalRequirement: Applied approval and Pause/Stop replay by operationId cause one effect.
tests.before: device allow_once on narrowed write expected 200.
tests.after: in-scope write; device allow_once 200 and replay unchanged; promoteStaged before COMPLETED is awaited.
tests.authorizationRationale: F02 D2 staging. The writes count still counts the staged succeeded run, which is 1.

tests.originalRequirement: Exactly one of the four racing answers wins; the losers are refused.
tests.before: every non-200 response code must be REFUSED.
tests.after: responses[0] (device allow_batch) must be non-200; losers must be REFUSED or WORKSTATION_REQUIRED; if a device allow_once wins it is promoted by the workstation before settle.
tests.authorizationRationale: Under the ask_every_time grant a device batch is refused outright (WORKSTATION_REQUIRED) or loses the race (REFUSED). The one-winner and single-effect checks are unchanged. This is a relaxation of the loser code, documented here.

addedNegativeRegressions: T9 F02 D3 (negative regression): a device cannot answer a write that the owner's narrowed Agent consent no longer covers
T9R F-02 narrowed consent: a device answer outside the Agent's current consent is refused and stages nothing
